FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Bulk Handling Systems and Equipment Sectional Committee had been approved by the Heavy Mechanical Engineering Division Council. In industries such as steel, thermal power, cement, etc, uniform quality of the~raw material plays an important role in the quality of the product and also for the optimum operation of the plant. The raw material is therefore first stacked, blended and then reclaimed for feeding to the plant for further processing. Reclaiming is done by reclaimers. Bucket wheel reclaimer is a type of reclaimer used for this purpose. Bucket wheel reclaimer consists of a system of belt conveyors and extendable boom on which a heel is fitted. The wheel has a number of buckets around it which dig into the pile of the material and loads it onto the conveyor system for feeding to the plant. For the purpose of deciding whcthcr a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, obscrvcd or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )`. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the spccificd value in this standard.

BULK HANDLING EQUIPMENT - BOOM TYPE BUCKET WHEEL RECLAIMER RAIL MOUNTED - DESIGN, MANUFACTURE AND ERECTION CODE OF PRACTICE
1 SCOPE

This standard covers mechanical, structural, inspection and testing requirements relating to design, manufacture and erection of rail mounted bucket wheel reclaimers. 2 REFERENCES The Indian Standards listed in Annex A are necessary adjuncts to this standard.
SECTION 1 MECHANICAL AND STRUCTURAL REQUlREMENTS 3 DESIGN REQUIREMENTS OF BUCKET WIIEEL RECLAIMER MECIIANISM

3.1.3 The reclaimer shall bc designed and manufactured to take care of the height, width and centre distance of stockpile(s) of specified parameters required by the~user. 3.1.4 The material of construction of the various parts of the reclaimer shall be suitable to handle the material specified. 3.1.5 Sclfety Against Overturning The safety against overturning shall be in accord- . ante with 11 of IS 13148 : 1991. 3.1.6 Safety Against Drifting The safety against drifting shall be in accordance with 12 of IS 13148 : 1991. 3.1.7 Safety Against Movement Due to the Wind Independent of the stability against overturning, a check shall be made that the reclaimer cannot bc set in motion by maximum wind increased by lOpercent.Thischeckshallbecarricdout assuming a coefficient of friction equal to 0.14 for braked wheels and a resistance to rolling of 35 N/IO kN for unbraked wheels mounted on antifriction bearings or of 100 N/15 kN for bushed wheels. For the design of clamps, the coefficient of friction between the clamps and the rail shall be taken as 0.25. Local push button stations shall bc provided near all drives for repair and maintenance. 3.2 Operating Requirements
3.2.1 Where so specified/rcquircd, the opcraiion of the various controls shall be automatic/semiautomatic/manual. Programmable logic controls (PLC) are recommended for automatic and scmiautomatic mode of operation. Howcvcr, in all casts manual override facility shall bc provided. All operations of the reclaimer including its long travel shall be controlled from the operator's cabin. Local push button stations shall be provided near all drives for repair and maintenance.

3.1 General
3.1.1 The main constituents of the reclaimer consists of: Drive mechanism; 1) Long travel, 2) Bucket wheel, 3) Boom conveyor, 4) Boom slcwing mechanism, 5) Boom luffing mechanism, 6) Cable reeling drum (CRD), and 7) Rail clamping. b) Under carriage; C> Tower structure/pylon/mast -with suspension; d) Bucket wheel; Bucket wheel boom; f) Machinery house; s) Operator's cabin; h) Communication and controls; j> Auxiliaries and accessories; 1) Dust control system, and 2) Counterweight.

3.1.2 The bucket wheel reclaimer shall be designed to take care of main, additional and special loads in accordance with IS 23145 : 1991.

IS 14416 : 1996 3.2.2 The operators cabin shall be pressurized so as to prevent ingress of dust for which a minimum water pressure of 5 mm water gauge shall be maintained inside the cabin. Keeping in view operator's comfort 15 air changes per hour shall be provided inside the cabin. 3.2.3 Dust control system shallbe provided so that the dust exit to atmosphere shall not exceed 150 mgm3 or the maximum statutory provisions for pollution control, whichever is less. The dusl so collected shall be fed back to the conveyor system of the reclaimer. 3.2.4 In case of wind velocity exceeding 72 km/h, an audio-visual signal shall bc given by the anemometer. Further if wind velocity exceeds 90 km/h, the total power shall be cut off and the electro-hydraulic rail clamps shall operate automatically. In addition, brakes shall be applied to all motions. 3.2.5 All drive limit switches shall be provided with additional back up switches and all brakes shall be fail safe type.

Rail sweeps to clear rails shall be provided in front of outer wheels. BufCcrs shall be provided on both sides of the carriage. 4.1.4 Jacking pads shall be provided for removal and changing of the wheels. 4.1.5 The rail gauge shall be decided after taking into consideration the technical parameter, design and the suitability of the machine 4.2 Boom Luffing The luffing of the cantilever boom shall bc with the help of winches/hoists/hydraulic mechanism. Suitable slow speed devices shall be provided during starting and also just bcforc the boom is latched automatically through a mechanical device. A positive limiting device shall be provided such that the luffing movement of the boom shall be possible only when the trolley and the operator's cabin are brought to the predetermined positions beyond the hinge point inside the tower. 4.3 Operator's Cabin 4.3.1 Operator's cabin with all necessary controls for performing the various operations shall be located in such a manner as to ensure complete view of the operations. Equalizing arrangements, if required, for cabin may be gravity hanging type or hydraulically operated. 4.3.2 The cabin shall be of adequate size to permit entry of and house all the required control cquipmcnt and may contain ample room for its adjustment and repair. The cabin shall face towards the ccntre line of the bucket wheel boom runway. 4.3.2.1 Control facilities for the following shall be provided in the cabin: Reclaimer travel, Trolley travel, b) Cabin lighting, Dust control system, and 4 An emergency stop button to switch `off all e) loader motions. This shall not interrupt power to the auxiliary circuits, lighting, signals, etc.

If so specified, suitable communication system shall also be provided between the reclaimer operator and local personnel. 3.2.7 Smoke detectors and fire extinguishers shall be provided at suitable locations. 3.2.8 Adequate illumination shall be provided near all drives, working/maintenance area of the machine, material discharge points, MCC rooms, platforms and walkways, staircases, ladders, etc, to enable operation/maintenance of the equipment. Sufficient number of emergency lights shall be provided at control room, exit points, ladders, etc, so that during power failure essential activities like switching off the controls and exit of personnel is possible. 4 DRIVE MECHANISM 4.1 Long Travel 4.1.1 The reclaimer shall be carried on double flanged track wheels arranged in equalizer for uniform distribution of loads. The travel motion shall comprise requisite number of motors, suitably synchronized. The four corners of the reclaimer shall be provided with resilient buffers to absorb \ the impact. In case of failure of one drive, it shall be possible to shift m~achine to repair/parking area, if required, by remaining pair of drives (may be at ' slower speeds). 2

4.3.3 Indicators and alarm for main supply, conphase trol supply, motions, wind pressure, failure, etc, shall be provided in the operator's cabin. 4.3.4 The cabin shall be provided with glazed windows on all sides to give operator an unobstructed

IS 14416 : 1996 view of the operations and for moving the reclaimer tower. Electrically operated wipers for the glass windows shall be provided to improve visibility during rains. 4.3.5 The cabin shall be furnished with sufficient facilities for comfortable seating of the operator with height adjustment. The cab shall be fully insulated and shall be equipped with wall mounted electric motor driven ventilating fan with gravity type louvers. (see nlso 3.2.2 and 8.1). 4.3.6 A signal horn controlled from the operator's cabin shall also be provided on the reclaimer. 4.4 Boom Conveyor The conveyor system for the boom conveyor shall generally be designed in accordance with IS 11592 : 1985. 5 MACHINERY ltIOUSE A machinery house accommodating drive mechanism for operating trolley travel, boom luffing and electrical equipment like switch gears, motor control centre, transformer, etc, shall be provided. Adequate space for maintenance and also maintenance facilities like hoist shall be provided inside machinery house wherever required. 6 BUCKET WHEEL 6.1 The bucket shape shall be designed as cell or cell less type depending `upon material characteristics and for proper culting clearance, taking wheel chamber into account for large bucket area for better emptying. The wheel shall be inclined towards the conveyors to increase wheel chute inclination and to achieve better emptying. The movement of the bucket shall be uniform and so timed that the reclaiming process, filling and discharge of the bucket operate with maximum efficiency. The flow of material shall be almost uniform and the end of discharge phase of the bucket shall coincide with the beginning of discharge phase of fbllowing bucket. 6.2 Buckets shall be made ofwear resistant steel or steel with wear resistant liners and fitted with replaceable, high abrasive resistant silicon manganese bucket teeth or tips onwear resistant bucket blade. Bucket wheel shall be driven by hydraulic motor or electric motor with hydraulic coupling through a reduction unit. The bucket wheel drive shall be independent of boom conveyor drive and equipped with a speed monitor as a safety facility on bucket wheel main gearing. 6.3 If required, bucket wheel assembly may have the provision for attaching harrow for blending of material.
3

6.4 Bucket wheel shall be driven through a torque limiting device to prevent overloading of the drive by switching off the drive in cast of jamming of the buckets in the stockpile. Brakes shall be provided on the bucket wheel drive so that wheei does not rotate when the power is off. 7 GENERAL DESIGN 7.1 Wire Ropes and Rope Drums Wire ropes shall conform to IS 2266 : 1989 and shall be of best plough steel. Keyways and splints shall conform to rclcvant Indian Standards. 7.5 Gears and Gearboxes Gears in power opcratcd motion shall be ground and hardened and shall conform to rclcvan 1 Indian Standards. Gearboxes shall have built in lubrication system of either splash or forced type. 7.6 Track Wheels 7.6.1 Trackwhcels may have cylindrical or taper-cd (conical) treads, with flnngcs or any other nicans as and where ncccssary, to guide the rcclaimcr cff'cctivcly and to prcvcnt dcrailmcnt. 11 LUBRICATION 11.1 Provision shall bc made for lubricating all bearings which shall be easily accessible from the working platforms of the reclaimer. 11.2 Preferably centralized group lubrication shall be provided. Where not feasible, group lubrication shall be provided. In any case provision shall be made at the bearings to prevent excess lubricant pressure. 11.3 Lubricating nipples, pipes and adapters shall gcncrally comply with relevant Indian Standards. 11.4 A lubricating chart shall be provided indicating all the lubricating points, the type of lubricant and rccommcndcd frequency of lubrication. 12 POWER FEEDING ARRAN~GEMRNTS 12.1 Power feeding to the reclaimers shall be through cable reeling drums (CRD) with trailing cable arrangements. Separate CRD for power and control cables shall be provided. The feeding of the cables to CRD shall be properly guided through cable guides to prevent the trailing cable fall on the track rails or entangle with fixed structures. Cable tray may be provided below the CRD along its path to prevent lying on the ground. However, the provisionofcables traysystem shall beoptionaland is not required in case level ground/floor is available below CRD for each cable to lie. ' 12.2 Safety limit switches/device to prcvcnt over stretching of cable at the feeding point on the ground shall be provided.

8.2 Adequate care shall be taken to avoid fouling of the discharge chute with skirt board provided on the boom conveyor during luffing motion. 8.3 Suitable liner(s) shall be provided for handling, abrasive material inside the discharge chute. 9 PRESSURIZATION SUPPRESSION 9.1 Pressurization Pressuring system shall bc provided to create a pressure of 5 mm water puge and 15 air changes per hour in the machinery house and operator's cabin. All electronic controls provided shall be housed in an airconditioned space. 9.2 Dust Control System 9.2.1 The dust control system shall be capable of suppressing effectively the dustwhich is raised from the receiving chute and also from all other material transfer points of the loading system up to but excluding the discharge point of the boom conveyor. Facility shall be provided to convey the dust collected to the material discharge point. 9.2.2 Maximum permissible dust loading from the system shall bc not more than 150 mg,Im' or the AND DUST

SECTION 15 GENERAL 15.1 The bucket wheel reclaimer shall becomplete with ail eiectrical accessories required for its safe, smooth and efficient operation. 2 ELECTRO-MECHANICAL REQUIREMENTS

conditions and to prevent inadvertent or accidental contact. 16.2 All enclosures shall preferably be of cast iron ot cast aluminium. Wherever sheet steel has to be used, the thickness of the metal shall not be less than 2 mm where enclosures are housed inside a covered area. All exposed outside panels shall have a metal thickness of not less than 3.15 mm. 16.2.1 All joints in enclosures shall be made dustproof by gaskets of high quality non-detcrioraling rubber or other suitable material. 16.3 Bare conductors, if used as bus wires, shall be iocated so as to prevent any form of accident contact. 15.3 Electrical syslem offered shall be suitable for the power supply system fault level at that point. 15.4 Electrical installation work shall be carried out through licensed electrical contractors, holding valid contractor's licences issued by the concerned Statutory Authority and also conforming to relevant standards of individual elcctricals located in Ihe machine. 15.5 All electricals shall be mounted on anti-vibration pad. 16 ENCLOSURE`S 16.1 All electrical equipments shall be properly enclosed or protected to suit the environmental

16.5 Wherever it is necessary for an electrical equipment to bc adjusted or inspected while in service, necessary clearances from live parts shall be provided to ensure safety in operation. 16.6 All enclosures of electrical equipments shall be given two coats of anti-corrosive epoxy paint over two coals of primer suitable for epoxy. 10

IS 14416 : 1996 16.7Various control gears like conductors, relays, control transformers, etc, shall be housed in dustproof, damp-proof and vermin-proof protective panels having doors interlocked with the supply control switches. Space heaters shall be provided for the panels. 17 POWER SUPPLY ARRANGEMENTS 17.1 Power supply shall be controlled by circuit breaker from which power shall be taken to the bucket wheel reclaimer through suitable collector systems such as cable reeling drums, etc. 17:2 It shall be possible to trip the shore-based circuit breaker from the machinery house of the reclaimer. 17.3 Circuit breaker to isolate the main supply to the reclaimer shall be provided. It shall be possible to switch off this breaker from the operator's cabin. 17.4 A plug and socket arrangement shall be provided to connect up the reclaimer's current collecting arrangements (power and control). 17.4.1 In case of plug and socket arrangements, power socket shall be interlocked so that the plug can be withdrawn only when the circuit breaker/ isolating switch is `OFF'. 17.5 External control links shall be taken out of the reclaimer using a current collection system similar to that for power. This system may carry the communication links also. 18 POWER TRANSFORMERS Power transformers if provided shall be dry type. They shall have overload, voltage and temperature protection. 19 MOTORS 19.1 To select a motor, the following shall be established: a) The maximum torque required to produce motic i "n the most unfavourable case. b) That 1 shall allow the reclaimer to perform its normal duty without abnormal wear. 19.2 AC motors shall be of totally enclosed, fan cooled, weather protected, hose-proof design (IP55 degree of protection) with atleast class B insulation. 19.2.1 AC motors shall have thermistor, load and short circuit protection. ovcr19.4 The motors shaI1 have atleast the following cyclic duty factors: 50 percent Bucket wheel 40 percent Boom conveyor Travel Slewing 40 percent 40 percent

19.4.1 Motors shall have built in thermistors with alarm and shall have space heating elements either winding heating or space heater elements as specified. 19.5 Thyristor drives if provided shall have current limitation, speed limitation, overload protection, short circuit protection and fuse protection and preferably rated for Class 4 duty. 20 RESISTORS Resistors if provided shall be intermittent rated for Class 4 duty and shall be suitable for the climatic conditions and the corrosive atmosphere described elsewhere. Stainless steel resist?tnce grids are preferred. 21 CABLES 21.1 All power cables shall be PVC insulated, armoured and PVC sheathed flexible type preferably with copper conductors. However, trailing cables shall have copper conductors only. All control cables shall be 2.5 mm* copper. 21.2 Power and control cables shall be protected with HRC fuses/circuit breakers. 21.3 The sizes of the cables shall be so chosen that they are rated to carry the full load current continuously after allowing for necessary dcrating factors for the conditions of installation, and also so that the voltage drop in cables shall not exceed 3 percent during running. 21.4 All cables shall be neatly clamped at suitable intervals. 21.5 All cables shall be terminated cable glands. by suitable

21.6 Metallic conduits shall be provided wherever necessary for the protection of the cables. 21.7 Power and control cables to the operator's cabin shall be provided with a loop to take care of movement of cabin during luff operations. 21.8 Electrical circuits may be printed/painted/ -pasted at the inside of control panel covers. 22 EARTIlING

19.3 DC motors shall have atleast IP-23 enclosure for indoor duty and IP-55 enclosure for outdoor duty. 11

22.1 The reclaimer shall be earthed through shoes rubbing on the rails. In addition, the

IS 14416:1996 connection between the circuit breaker and the reclaimer shall have a fourth conductor to be used as an earth connection.This earth connection shall be linked to the earth connection of the main circuit breaker. 22.2 Double equipments. 23 LIGIITING 23.1 The reclaimer shall be provided with suitable illumination to ensure good lighting at all places. 23.2 Flood lights shall be provided at the following points. a) On the operator's cabin for the operator to see the bucket operation during the night. h) In front and rear portions of the reclaimer to properly light the tracks during reclaimer travel in the night. 23.3 All lighting circuits shall be protected with HRC fuses and shall be controlled by one main switch fuse in addition to separate circuit control switches. 23.4 Battery operated emergency lights shall be provided at strategic locations. These shall be the automatic type. The light shall automatically come `ON' when normal power supply fails and shall go `OFF' automatically when normal supply comes back. The unit shall incorporate a trickle charger for keeping the battery on charge. The battery shall be rated for atleast 30 minutes operation. 23.5 Air-craft warning/obstructions lights shall beprovidcd on the reclaimer if rcquircd by any Statutory Authority for which separate battery units with chargers shall be provided. 23.6 All light fittings shall be mounted on shock absorbers. 23.7. Low voltage (24 V) plug and socket outlets, with hand lamps and sufficient lengths of cables shall bc provided. 24 CONTROLS A safe low voltage shall be employed for the controls. This shall be from the secondary winding of an isolating transformer. One terminal of this supply shall be earthed and the contactor and the relay coils shall be connected to this terminal. earthing shall be provided for all 25 INTERLOCKS 25.1 Necesary interlocks for the safe and smooth operation of the-reclaimer shall be provided. 25.2 `Forward' and `Reverse' contactors shall be interlocked electrically and preferably mechanically as well. 26 PROTECTION 26.1 In case of wind speed beyond preset level, an audio-visual alarm shall be given in operator's cabin to enable the operator to stop the operation of the machine. If the operation is not stopped , automatic cut-off of power supp~ly shall be effective beyond a preset higher wind speed. 26.2 Shunt and series limit switches shall be provided for all motions. The shunt switch shall operate first and if the motion fails to stop, series limit switch shall act. Additional limit switches shall be provided for long travel, slewing, etc. 26.2.1 Instead of shunt and series limit switches, mechanical type end-limit switches may be provided. The pre-limit switch shall act first to trip the motor and apply mechanical brakes. On reaching the end-limit switch, the breaker on the secondary side of the transformer shall get tripped. 26.3 Phase failure relay shall be provided to trip the main circuit breaker. 26.4 A warning audio-alarm shall be given automatically during long travel operation. 27 AIR CONDITIONING In the interest of long life and reliable operation, electronic components and other components sensitive to temperature, humidity and dust, shall prcfcrably be located in air conditioned space(s). 28 COMM~UNICATION FACILITIES Inter-communication recommended. 29 AUTOMATION Where considered essential, automation may be provided to rcducc physical and psychological stress of operator. Provision shall be kept for overriding automation. facility within structure is
